$comment: The reference tasks of the conformance harness (evals/README.md). Each prompt is written the way a product team asks for a screen: it names the need, never a component. `gold` points at the code that answers it in the design system: the `## Code example` of a page pattern or of a component spec. `render` is the JSX that mounts a pattern example whose export takes props. `base` makes a task a change to an existing screen: the generator receives that file with the prompt, and the gold is the screen once changed. `"default": false` keeps a task out of the default run: it runs only when a suite or `--tasks` names it, so adding it leaves the 26 tasks the recorded runs and the budgets compare unchanged. `suites` names subsets of the tasks: `skills` is the one the agent skills are measured on (`--suite skills`).

tasks.prompt: Build the sign-in page of our web app: email and password, a link to recover a forgotten password, and a way to create an account for people who don't have one. Show a clear message when the email and password don't match.
Add a way to create a new project from the projects page: a button that opens a short form with the project name and an optional description, and confirms once the project exists.
Add a delete action for a project called "Website redesign". Deleting can't be undone, so the person must confirm it first, and they should be told once it's done.
Build the project details screen where someone can change the project's name, description and visibility, and save the changes only when they choose to.
Our projects list is empty for new users. Design what they see instead of a blank page, with a way to create their first project.
Add filters above the projects list: by status (active, paused, archived) and by owner, with a way to clear them, and show how many projects match. There are 12 matching projects right now.
Build the form where a new user sets up their account: full name, email, role, and a short bio. Tell them what each field expects and what to fix when a value is wrong.
Show what the projects grid looks like while the project cards are still loading.
Build the layout of the projects area of our app: a side navigation with the main sections, the current page highlighted, and a header that says where the person is.
Build the profile form (name and email) with a save button that tells the person while it's saving, when it's saved, and what to do if saving fails.
Add a search box over a list of projects (Apollo, Borealis, Cassini, Discovery) that narrows the list as the person types, and says so plainly when nothing matches.
Build the settings page of our app, with sections for the profile, notifications and appearance (light or dark theme).
Show the list of recent invoices — number, status, payment method and amount — with a total at the bottom.
Add page navigation under a long list of search results: previous and next, the page numbers around the current one, and a gap for the pages in between.
Add a chart to the dashboard that compares desktop and mobile visitors over the last six months.
Build the app shell: a collapsible side navigation with the main sections and the signed-in user at the bottom, next to the page content.
Add a quick-actions palette where people type to find a page or an action and run it from the keyboard.
Split the account screen into two views, account details and password, that the person switches between without leaving the page.
Let the person pick a delivery date on a month calendar.
Show the files attached to a message — their names, sizes and upload progress — and let the person remove one.
Build the conversation view of a support chat: the messages from both sides, kept scrolled to the latest one as new messages arrive.
Add a FAQ section where each question opens to show its answer.
Add the menu that opens from the user's avatar in the header, with their profile, settings and a way to sign out.
Build the step where the person types the six-digit code we sent them by text message.
People should pick a plan when they set up their account: Starter or Team, with Starter chosen by default. Add that choice to this form.

Add notification preferences to this settings page: a weekly summary of their projects every Monday, on by default, and an email when someone mentions them. Each preference should take effect as soon as it's changed.
When the email and password don't match, this sign-in page stays as it was and people can't tell what went wrong. Tell them clearly when that happens.
This button deletes the project "Website redesign" on the first click, and a deletion can't be undone. Make the person confirm before it happens.
Add a way to clear these filters in one step, and show how many projects match them: 12 right now.
This save button gives no feedback. Tell the person while their changes are saving, once they're saved, and what to do if saving fails.
When nothing matches the search, the list just goes blank. Say so plainly and give the person a way out.
People can't take back what they typed in this form before they save. Add a way to discard their changes, and tell them once the changes are saved.
